title: One-step Optimal Transport via Regularized Distribution Matching Distillation

claims.text: Theorem 3.1 proves that as the transport-cost regularization weight lambda approaches 0, the RDMD objective's optimum converges to the Monge optimal transport map under quadratic cost and mild regularity conditions (Section 3.2, Theorem 3.1).

The RDMD training objective (Section 3.1) combines a KL-divergence distribution-matching term between perturbed real/fake diffusion distributions with an explicit transport-cost regularization term lambda*E[c(x, G(x))], optimized via coordinate descent over the generator and a fake diffusion model (Section 3.1).

On the AFHQv2 Cat-to-Wild 64x64 unpaired translation task, RDMD attains an FID of 6.9, compared to 2.0 for the pretrained (non-distilled) diffusion teacher, while achieving strictly higher SSIM and near-strictly higher PSNR than baselines including ILVR, SDEdit, and EGSDE (Section 5.2, Figure 4).

A toy 2D experiment (single Gaussian to 8-Gaussian mixture) shows that setting the regularization weight lambda=0.2 balances distribution-matching fidelity against input-output correspondence, reducing trajectory intersections relative to unregularized distillation (Section 5.1).

Appendix A gives a formal gamma-convergence proof that the RDMD objective converges to the hard-constrained Monge problem, supporting the claimed asymptotic optimality of the one-step generator (Appendix A).
